label: Standards, Taxonomy and Market Architecture
definition: Design, governance, mapping, architecture, licensing, and technical delivery of controlled classifications and market-operating languages used to connect needs, capabilities, evidence, responses, decisions, and outcomes.

families.label: Standards and Taxonomy Engineering
families.definition: Development, governance, and mapping of controlled classification systems, standards, and semantic market structures.

capabilities.label: Taxonomy development
capabilities.definition: The organizational ability to design, document, maintain, and version structured classification systems, including hierarchies, identifiers, preferred labels, definitions, relationships, and editorial rules.

capabilities.label: Standards governance
capabilities.definition: The organizational ability to establish and administer authority, review, change control, release, integrity, conflict, and stakeholder-participation rules for a governed standard.

capabilities.label: Capability mapping
capabilities.definition: The organizational ability to map market needs, organizational abilities, and external classifications to controlled capability concepts while preserving scope, provenance, confidence, and semantic relationships.

families.label: Evidence, Response and Decision Architecture
families.definition: Design of structured evidence, response, and evaluation systems that connect requirements to submissions and transparent decisions.

capabilities.label: Evidence architecture
capabilities.definition: The organizational ability to design structured evidence, credential, verification, provenance, recency, sufficiency, and coverage models used to establish fitness, eligibility, or compliance.

capabilities.label: Response architecture
capabilities.definition: The organizational ability to design reusable response sections, templates, instructions, dependencies, and data structures that govern how market participants answer requests.

capabilities.label: Decision architecture
capabilities.definition: The organizational ability to design gates, scored factors, weights, formulas, evidence links, and decision rules used to evaluate alternatives transparently and consistently.

families.label: Standards Licensing and Technical Delivery
families.definition: Commercial licensing and machine-readable delivery of governed taxonomies, schemas, releases, mappings, and validation services.

capabilities.label: Controlled taxonomy licensing
capabilities.definition: The organizational ability to license governed taxonomy content, schemas, releases, and permitted derivative uses under defined rights, restrictions, attribution, version, and distribution terms.

capabilities.label: Taxonomy API delivery
capabilities.definition: The organizational ability to provide versioned taxonomy, mapping, search, validation, and release data through documented application programming interfaces or other machine-readable delivery services.
